clue.text: Looking for ruler of the waves, say?

indicators.note: say tells the solver to go by how the phrase is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a sea king is a monarch of the ocean, such as Neptune

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for the monarch who rules the oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seeking something is to be searching for it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Puzzle page introduced by problem about time

indicators.note: introduced by means preceded by, so the letter for page comes last
about means surrounding, so the word for problem goes round the letter for time

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A puzzle page opened by a question concerning time.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to baffle or puzzle them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cooked sole apt to need sprinkling of salt and dressing

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so these letters are rearranged
a sprinkling scatters, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fish dish that needs a pinch of salt and a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' makes ELASTOP from SOLE APT, and 'sprinkling of' makes LAST from SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: This brand of sticking plaster is a wound dressing, the British name for an adhesive bandage.

clue.text: In anger, I pass opinion on head

parts.note: to rate something is to judge or assess it
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Someone furious, delivering a verdict on their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: A NESS is a headland, a common element in British place names such as Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irate means being angry, so the noun form is a state of wrath.

clue.text: Completes course in GCSE English: does that badly …

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words in and GCSE as written, with English abbreviated to E

explanation.surface: A pupil finishing their schooling, doing poorly in the English exam.
explanation.walkthrough: GCSE is the exam English pupils sit at about sixteen.
explanation.definitionFit: To go the full distance is an idiom for finishing a race or task, lasting to the end.

clue.text: One works on loom, we state

parts.note: to aver is to state or declare firmly

explanation.surface: A group claiming that somebody labours at a loom.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes cloth by interlacing threads on a loom is the classic textile worker.

clue.text: … undoubtedly, if exam paper is so untypical?

definitions.text: if exam paper is so untypical
definitions.meaning: a test sheet with no queries on it would be very unusual

explanation.surface: Following on from the clue before: certainly, an exam with no questions would be odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for certainly, and literally describes a paper lacking any queries.

clue.text: Liberal — a politician first in local elections

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat candidate, an MP, coming first in council voting.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Writer from the continent

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are drawn from inside these words

explanation.surface: An author from mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a European author, and Umberto Eco is one, but the letters come from inside 'the continent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto Eco, the Italian novelist of The Name of the Rose, is a famous author.

clue.text: Mischief-maker taking brief gamble on jail

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little sprite

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a risk is a gamble

explanation.surface: A troublemaker having a quick bet on whether he ends up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To jail someone is to lock them up, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Foreign article about a battle in the dark

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article
a war is a large-scale battle or conflict

explanation.surface: An overseas newspaper piece on a conflict fought at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark is an idiom for lacking knowledge, ignorant of the facts.

clue.text: Thanks for order in part of pub

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
pro means in favour of, so for
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Gratitude for an order placed in a section of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar-room in an inn where drinks are served from casks is one area of a public house.

clue.text: Film company's minor hit cut, alienating west

parts.note: a pat is a light tap

indicators.note: alienating means sending away, so the letter for west is dropped

parts.note: to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A film studio's small success gets edited down and loses its western audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The French firm founded by the Pathé brothers was a pioneering cinema studio and newsreel maker.

clue.text: Gardener sometimes misused wet roller

indicators.note: something misused is handled wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden roller, wet and used improperly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone using a small hand trowel is, on occasion, a gardener; the 'sometimes' marks an example.

clue.text: Bloomer Stalin movie corrected

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mistake in a film about Stalin, since put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it is something that blooms: a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella damascena is a garden flower, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Travellers about now meeting locals leaving their capital

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the present is now

indicators.note: leaving their capital means the locals' word loses its opening letter

parts.note: natives are local people

explanation.surface: Tourists arriving at present and meeting residents who have left the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving their capital' drops N, the first letter of NATIVES, leaving ATIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales reps are commercial travellers who journey around selling goods for a firm.

clue.text: Scottish town brother outwardly ignored, for example

indicators.note: ignoring the outside means dropping the first and last letters of the word brother

parts.note: say is used like for example

explanation.surface: A sibling being snubbed in a town in Scotland, to give an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main town on the Isle of Bute in western Scotland.

clue.text: Coach perhaps controlled competitive game after tense start

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the other pieces follow the opening letter
the start of the word tense is its opening letter

parts.note: ran means managed or controlled
a sport is a competitive game

explanation.surface: A sports coach who ran a match after a nervous beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer, but it is a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is an example of a vehicle that carries people, which the question mark flags.

clue.text: A foreign naturist (not European) in disguise, wanting change of appearance

indicators.note: in disguise means the letters are presented in altered form
not means without, so the letter for European is removed

explanation.surface: An overseas nudist, not from Europe, going about disguised and wanting a new look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not European' removes E from FOREIGN, giving FORIGN; with A and NATURIST these letters are shuffled by 'in disguise'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfiguration is a complete transformation of form or look, as in the biblical scene.

clue.text: Reckons one million can be housed in property developments

indicators.note: being housed in something means sitting within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: housing estates are property developments
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone calculating that a million people could live in new housing projects.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to reckon roughly, judging an amount without exact figures.

clue.text: Complain endlessly about cold and hot coffee

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened complaint goes round the other letters
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to moan is to complain
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Grumbling non-stop about coffee being cold, then hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts MOAN to MOA, which goes about CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of fine coffee, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Refuse to move accommodation for horse

definitions.meaning: to stop and not go forward, as an engine or a stubborn animal does
a stable compartment for one animal

explanation.surface: A horse that won't budge from its box.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to stop dead and a single compartment in a stable.

clue.text: Port archipelago surely protects

indicators.note: protects means holds within, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: An island chain that surely shields its harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is the major seaport of Nigeria on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Father and I are able to accompany a fellow from 20?

indicators.note: accompanying means going alongside, so these pieces sit next to the letter a

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
can means are able to

explanation.surface: A dad and his child able to escort a visitor from Lagos.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the down answer LAGOS, the Nigerian port; someone from there is from that continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Lagos in Nigeria is a native of that continent; the query marks the example.

clue.text: Steal short dress

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a robe is a long dress or gown

explanation.surface: Pinching a skimpy frock.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob is to take by theft, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: I grin awkwardly, keeping on doing some housework

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the scrambled letters hold the word on
awkwardly means clumsily, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smiling uncomfortably while carrying on with household chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' turns I GRIN into IRING, and 'keeping' puts ON inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot iron is one of the standard household chores.

clue.text: Burning book in a lounge

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter for book goes within the other words

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about

explanation.surface: A book catches fire in a sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire with flames is aflame, burning fiercely.

clue.text: Symbolically writes refusal to family of philanthropists?

parts.note: no is a refusal
the Tates were sugar refiners; Sir Henry Tate founded the Tate gallery

explanation.surface: Someone putting a rejection to a wealthy charitable dynasty in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set down music or similar in a system of symbols.
